questions.question: [Additive Manufacturing] Q: Why is additive manufacturing described as producing minimal waste compared to CNC machining?
questions.correctAnswer: Additive processes only deposit material where the component exists, so nearly all material becomes the finished part. CNC machining starts with a solid block and removes material (as chips/swarf) to carve the shape, wasting significant raw material.
questions.explanation: Additive processes only deposit material where the component exists, so nearly all material becomes the finished part. CNC machining starts with a solid block and removes material (as chips/swarf) to carve the shape, wasting significant raw material.

questions.question: [Aerodynamics in Engineering] Q: Explain how an aerofoil generates lift using Bernoulli's principle.
questions.correctAnswer: The aerofoil's curved upper surface forces air to travel faster than the flatter lower surface. According to Bernoulli's principle, faster-moving air has lower pressure. The pressure difference (lower above, higher below) creates an upward force — lift — that supports the aircraft.
questions.explanation: The aerofoil's curved upper surface forces air to travel faster than the flatter lower surface. According to Bernoulli's principle, faster-moving air has lower pressure. The pressure difference (lower above, higher below) creates an upward force — lift — that supports the aircraft.

questions.question: [Aerodynamics in Engineering] Q: Why does drag increase significantly at higher speeds?
questions.correctAnswer: Drag force is proportional to the square of velocity: Fd = 0.5 x Cd x A x rho x v2. Doubling speed quadruples drag, meaning much more thrust (and fuel) is needed to overcome air resistance at high speeds.
questions.explanation: Drag force is proportional to the square of velocity: Fd = 0.5 x Cd x A x rho x v2. Doubling speed quadruples drag, meaning much more thrust (and fuel) is needed to overcome air resistance at high speeds.

questions.question: [Aerodynamics in Engineering] Q: Explain two ways a car manufacturer can reduce aerodynamic drag.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Streamlining the body shape with a smooth, tapered rear to reduce flow separation and turbulence (lowering form drag). 2) Flattening the underbody and adding a rear diffuser to reduce air turbulence beneath the car, which contributes significantly to overall drag.
questions.explanation: 1) Streamlining the body shape with a smooth, tapered rear to reduce flow separation and turbulence (lowering form drag). 2) Flattening the underbody and adding a rear diffuser to reduce air turbulence beneath the car, which contributes significantly to overall drag.

questions.question: [Composites & Other Materials] Q: Explain what a composite material is and why composites are used in engineering.
questions.correctAnswer: A composite combines a matrix and a reinforcement to create properties that neither material has alone. The reinforcement provides strength and stiffness while the matrix binds, protects and transfers loads. Composites allow engineers to tailor properties for specific applications.
questions.explanation: A composite combines a matrix and a reinforcement to create properties that neither material has alone. The reinforcement provides strength and stiffness while the matrix binds, protects and transfers loads. Composites allow engineers to tailor properties for specific applications.

questions.question: [Composites & Other Materials] Q: Why does fibre orientation matter in composite materials?
questions.correctAnswer: Unidirectional fibres provide maximum strength only along the fibre direction; loads perpendicular to the fibres are carried only by the weaker matrix. Woven or multidirectional reinforcement distributes strength in multiple directions, which is needed when loads are not all in one direction.
questions.explanation: Unidirectional fibres provide maximum strength only along the fibre direction; loads perpendicular to the fibres are carried only by the weaker matrix. questions.question: [Electrical Systems] Q: Explain how a relay works and why relays are used in engineering control systems.
questions.correctAnswer: A small control current flows through the relay coil, creating a magnetic field that pulls in the armature, switching the contacts. This allows a low-voltage, low-current control circuit to safely switch a high-voltage, high-current load circuit, providing isolation and safety.
questions.explanation: A small control current flows through the relay coil, creating a magnetic field that pulls in the armature, switching the contacts. questions.question: [Electrical Systems] Q: Calculate the current drawn by a 2.2 kW heater connected to a 230V mains supply.
questions.correctAnswer: I = P / V = 2200 / 230 = 9.57 A. A 13A fuse would be appropriate for this appliance.
questions.explanation: I = P / V = 2200 / 230 = 9.57 A. A 13A fuse would be appropriate for this appliance.

questions.question: [Electrical Systems] Q: Explain the difference between AC and DC power supplies, giving an application for each.
questions.correctAnswer: AC reverses direction periodically (mains 230V 50Hz for household and industrial equipment). DC flows in one direction only (batteries for portable electronics and vehicles).
questions.explanation: AC reverses direction periodically (mains 230V 50Hz for household and industrial equipment). DC flows in one direction only (batteries for portable electronics and vehicles).
